01_intro: This is the Museum of Modern Art's nineteen twenty-nine loan exhibition catalogue, one of seven hundred and fifty-seven [MoMA](/ˈmoʊmə/) catalogues in my scanned library. Seventy-seven thousand pages. No catalogue knows which pictures are inside them, and a scan with no text layer can't even say what book it is. [Colophon](/ˈkɑləfɑn/) reads them the way an art librarian would, with two Meta models.
02_sam: SAM three point one runs locally, on two D.G.X. Sparks and a Windows P.C. with a forty-ninety: eight text prompts per page, from painting to map. Nine water towers become nine boxes; the thirty-one prints of an installation, thirty-one. All seventy-seven thousand pages went through in five hours with zero failures: ninety-three thousand figures.
03_reader: Then Muse Spark reads each page once, with the figures numbered. For every box it returns what it depicts and the printed caption, split into artist, title, year, medium and credit, and says whether the box is a figure at all. One call per page, strict [JSON](/ˈdʒeɪsɑn/), about half a cent.
04_search: Everything the model read is embedded and searchable in plain words. A woman reading a letter: [Seurat's](/sɜˈɹɑz/) drawing from the nineteen twenty-nine catalogue, [Lautrec's](/loʊˈtɹɛks/) Reading from nineteen thirty-one. Each hit opens its page with the figure outlined, the record, the caption as printed, and a link to the exact page of [MoMA's](/ˈmoʊməz/) own P.D.F. A city street at night: Van Gogh's café terrace, a [Bauhaus](/ˈbaʊhaʊs/) building after dark.
05_works: Because the captions are read, not guessed, the same work can be followed across catalogues: Picasso's Green Still Life was reproduced six times between nineteen thirty-one and nineteen thirty-six, [Redon's](/ɹəˈdɔnz/) Silence five times. Fifty-three catalogues are indexed so far; the pipeline is built for all seven hundred and fifty-seven, I stopped at the budget.
06_identifier: The identifier reads a book's title page, copyright page and last pages, and returns a catalogue record. Nothing is guessed: a field not printed on the pages sent comes back empty, with a note. Every I.S.B.N. is checksum-tested, and a record is verified only when Open Library's title for it matches the title page. On all seven hundred and fifty-seven catalogues, scored against [MoMA's](/ˈmoʊməz/) own record sheet, page one of every P.D.F., withheld from the model: title ninety-four percent, year ninety, publisher eighty-six, author eighty-five, I.S.B.N. ninety-two. And this brochure is dated nineteen eighty-seven in [MoMA's](/ˈmoʊməz/) record; the model read the copyright line, two thousand and five, and the exhibition dates agree.
07_cost: The whole run cost thirty-nine dollars on the Meta Model A.P.I., under a hundred-dollar cap enforced from the files: the reader checks the spend before every call, and an independent guard stops everything at ninety-eight. The code, every number, and the list of the seven hundred and fifty-seven [MoMA](/ˈmoʊmə/) P.D.Fs to rebuild it are on GitHub.
08_close: [Colophon](/ˈkɑləfɑn/). A library that knows what is on its pages.
